style.vernacular: Sand-coloured low and mid-rise reinforced-concrete buildings in cream and beige render and limestone cladding, flat roofs with parapets, small recessed windows and screens for shade; villas and compounds behind high walls; heritage-style buildings with plastered coral-stone walls, exposed timber pole ends and battlement parapets; a skyline of reflective blue-glass towers in West Bay and sculptural landmark buildings in Education City, Msheireb and the Corniche; palms and irrigated lawns.
style.ornament: Islamic geometric screens and mashrabiya-pattern cladding; pointed and round arches; battlement (merlon) parapets on heritage-style buildings; carved gypsum screens and niches; exposed round timber poles (danchal) in souq-style buildings; blue-and-gold tile accents on mosques; sculptural landmarks inspired by desert rose, dhow sail and fanar lantern.

sources.what: traditional Qatari architecture: courtyards, flat roofs, small windows, limestone and coral slabs with gypsum plaster, arches, niches and battlements; modern landmarks in Education City

desert-rose form of 539 interlocking discs clad in glass-fibre reinforced concrete
